$comment: Whole patches derived from worked examples -- the ARP 2600 owner's manual's
patch section, and Strange's chapters on voices built from these parts.
THE FILE IS PROVENANCE; THE FAMILY IS TAXONOMY. Every record here declares
its own `family`, so a bell goes to texture and a self-oscillating filter
goes to voice, whatever book they arrived in. Filing them under where they
were found instead would group them by the one property nobody browsing the
library is looking for. Where each came from is in `source`, which is where
THE 2600 WAS NORMALLED AND A RACK IS NOT. Its worked patches assume a set
of connections the instrument had already made -- the keyboard to the
oscillators, the oscillators to the filter, the filter to the amplifier --
and describe only the cables you add on top. Translated to an unnormalled
rack, every one of those assumed connections becomes a requirement, which
is why several records here look longer than the patch they came from.
Techniques and facts are not anybody's property; the words are ours.

idioms.is: Two oscillators multiplied to give an inharmonic spectrum, then struck: the sum and difference tones belong to no scale, and an envelope on the filter gives them an attack and a decay.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the strike reads as metal — a definite attack, a long inharmonic ring, and no clear sense of a single note.
idioms.source: The ARP 2600 owner's manual's ring-modulator patches

topology.describe: one oscillator has to be the carrier
the other has to multiply it at audio rate — that multiplication is where the inharmonic partials come from
the multiplied signal has to reach a filter, which is the bell's body
an envelope has to strike it — without one the inharmonic spectrum simply drones, which is a texture and not a bell
the result has to reach the audio path

listen_for.sounds_like: a struck bell or gong: a bright clangorous attack that decays into a smaller number of ringing partials, none of which agrees with the others about what note this is
listen_for.confusable_with: a detuned pair, which beats but stays harmonic; if you can hum the note, the two oscillators are being summed rather than multiplied

expect.why: an inharmonic spectrum should defeat a pitch tracker for much of the run; a confidently tracked pitch throughout is evidence the multiplication is not happening

common_mistakes.message: nothing multiplies at audio rate, so the spectrum stays harmonic and this is a filtered tone
nothing strikes it, so the bell drones instead of ringing
no carrier passes through the multiplier
the multiplied signal never reaches the filter

implies: use the rack as an effect
idioms.is: Audio brought in from outside the rack, processed, and sent back out, so the rack acts on a sound it did not generate.
idioms.sounds_right_when: you recognise the incoming sound and hear what the rack did to it.
idioms.source: The ARP 2600 owner's manual's external-input and preamp patches

topology.describe: the interface's input has to reach something — an audio interface is a way IN as well as a way out, and this is the half people forget
the processed signal has to go back out, or the rack is listening and saying nothing

listen_for.sounds_like: the source, still identifiable, wearing whatever the rack put on it — if you cannot tell what went in, the processing has gone too far to be called processing
listen_for.confusable_with: a patch that generates its own sound and happens to have an interface in it

common_mistakes.message: no external audio reaches the rack
the processed signal never returns to the output

implies: filter with nothing going into it
idioms.is: A resonant filter with nothing patched into its audio input, played by voltage at its cutoff: the resonance itself is the sound, which is a near-sine tone with no oscillator in the patch.
idioms.sounds_right_when: you hear a pure, slightly unstable sine whose pitch follows the cutoff voltage.
idioms.source: The ARP 2600 owner's manual, on running the filter's resonance up until it sings

topology.describe: a voltage has to play the cutoff, because the cutoff IS the pitch here
the filter's output has to reach an amplifier
an envelope has to open the amplifier, or the tone never stops
the amplifier has to reach the audio path

forbidden_topology.describe: nothing may be patched into the filter's audio input — the moment something is, this is an ordinary filtered voice and the resonance is a colour rather than the sound

listen_for.sounds_like: a clean sine that is not quite clean: it wavers slightly, it does not track pitch perfectly across the range, and it thins out at the extremes in a way an oscillator does not
listen_for.confusable_with: an oscillator through a resonant filter, which is steadier and richer; the tell is that this one has no oscillator to turn off

expect.why: a self-oscillating filter is close to a pure sine, so a pitch tracker should hold onto it for most of the run

common_mistakes.message: something is patched into the filter's audio input, so the resonance is filtering a sound rather than being one
nothing plays the cutoff, so the tone sits on one pitch
the filter never reaches an amplifier

idioms.is: Noise through an amplifier opened by an envelope that an unpredictable source fires, so the texture arrives in bursts nobody can anticipate.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the bursts are clearly separate events and their spacing has no pattern you can hold onto.
idioms.source: The ARP 2600 owner's manual's noise and sample-and-hold patches

topology.describe: noise has to pass through the amplifier
an unpredictable source has to fire the envelope — a steady clock here gives a rhythm, which is a different patch
the envelope has to open the amplifier, or the noise runs continuously
the gated noise has to reach the audio path

listen_for.sounds_like: handfuls of gravel, or rain on a roof: separate events, each one broadband, arriving at intervals you cannot predict or tap along with
listen_for.confusable_with: continuous filtered noise, which has no events in it at all

expect.why: if the bursts lock to a strong pulse, something steady is firing the envelope and the chance source is not reaching it

common_mistakes.message: nothing gates the noise, so it runs continuously instead of arriving in bursts
nothing fires the envelope, so there are no bursts
no noise passes through the amplifier

idioms.is: A trigger sent into a resonant filter's audio input, so each pulse excites the resonance and rings out as a pitched blip — a percussive voice with no oscillator and no envelope.
idioms.sounds_right_when: each hit is a short pitched ring whose pitch is the cutoff and whose length is the resonance.
idioms.source: Standard practice with a resonant filter; the same excitation idea as a struck string

topology.describe: the trigger has to go into the filter's AUDIO input — into the cutoff it is a sweep, and nothing rings
the filter has to reach the audio path

listen_for.sounds_like: a woodblock or a tuned drum: a click with a pitched tail, the tail getting longer as resonance rises until it stops being a hit and starts being a note
listen_for.confusable_with: an oscillator with a short envelope, which has a body the whole way through; a ping is almost all decay

expect.why: a ping decays to nothing between hits; sound present for nearly the whole run means the resonance is set high enough to be a drone

common_mistakes.message: nothing strikes the filter, so there is nothing to ring
the filter never reaches the audio path

implies: fm that gets brighter on the attack
idioms.is: Audio-rate frequency modulation whose depth is itself opened by an envelope, so each note starts rich in sidebands and settles toward the carrier as the envelope falls.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the attack is markedly brighter and more complex than the sustain, without a filter anywhere in the patch.
idioms.source: Strange on modulation index as the parameter that governs an FM timbre

axis.position: audio rate, with the depth itself under an envelope
axis.set_by: the modulator's rate and the amount of it reaching the carrier's frequency input — two knobs, and every position on this axis patches from an oscillator to a frequency input
axis.$comment: One structure, three sounds. Below hearing the movement is heard AS movement, which is vibrato; above it the same cable produces sidebands, which is FM; and putting the depth under an envelope makes the timbre an event rather than a setting. A checker reading cables sees one technique, which is why these are three records on one axis rather than one skeleton.

topology.describe: the modulator has to pass through an amplifier — that amplifier is the index
an envelope has to open it, or the index is a knob and every note has the same brightness
the gated modulation has to reach a carrier's frequency input
the carrier has to reach the audio path

listen_for.sounds_like: a brass-like note: a bright, slightly harsh attack that mellows into a much simpler sustain, all of it happening with no filter in the patch
listen_for.confusable_with: an envelope on a filter, which removes harmonics that were there; this adds harmonics that were not

expect.why: the index sweep should move the brightness by at least a half-octave; less than that and the envelope is barely reaching the amplifier

common_mistakes.message: nothing opens the index amplifier, so every note has the same brightness
the gated modulation never reaches a carrier, so there is no FM
no modulator passes through the index amplifier

implies: the filter opens when it gets loud
idioms.is: A signal's own loudness converted to a control voltage and used to open the filter it is passing through, so the sound opens itself on every attack.
idioms.sounds_right_when: louder moments are brighter, and the brightness follows the playing rather than a clock.
idioms.source: Strange on envelope following as a source of control voltage

topology.describe: audio has to reach the follower
the followed level has to open the filter — that link is the entire technique
audio has to pass through the filter it is opening, or the patch is following one thing and brightening another

listen_for.sounds_like: the sound opening on each attack and closing as it dies away — the timbre tied to the dynamics rather than to any clock
listen_for.confusable_with: an envelope on the filter, which opens by the same amount every time regardless of how loud the note is

expect.why: if the brightness barely moves, the follower's output is not reaching the cutoff with any range

common_mistakes.message: the followed level never reaches the filter
no audio reaches the follower
no audio passes through the filter being opened

idioms.is: An oscillator's output returned to its own frequency input, so it modulates itself and its waveform becomes something no waveform switch offers.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the tone is harsh and continuous, and small changes in the return amount change its character completely.
idioms.source: Strange on feedback applied to a control input

topology.describe: the oscillator's output has to reach its OWN frequency input — a second oscillator doing it is ordinary FM
the oscillator has to reach the audio path

listen_for.sounds_like: a raw, buzzing tone that gets thicker and less stable as the return rises, eventually losing its pitch altogether
listen_for.confusable_with: a waveshaper, which adds harmonics predictably; self-modulation goes unstable and does not come back gracefully

common_mistakes.message: the oscillator does not modulate itself, so this is a plain waveform
the oscillator never reaches the audio path

implies: each note chooses the next pitch
idioms.is: A cycling function generator that samples a new pitch every time it finishes, so the patch plays a melody it decides on as it goes, one note at a time.
idioms.sounds_right_when: notes arrive continuously, each at a new pitch, with nobody having written the sequence.
idioms.source: Standard function-generator practice; the same self-clocking loop as the krell patch, with the sampled voltage choosing pitch rather than duration

topology.describe: the generator has to retrigger itself, or the patch plays one note and stops
the end of each note has to take a new sample — that is what makes the melody self-generated rather than sequenced
the held voltage has to reach a pitch input
the generator has to open an amplifier, or the notes run together into a glide

listen_for.sounds_like: an unbroken line of separate notes at unrelated pitches, evenly spaced unless something is randomising the generator's time as well
listen_for.confusable_with: a krell, where what the sampled voltage sets is the DURATION; if the pitches repeat and the timing wanders, the cable is on the wrong input

expect.why: the sampled voltage should reach at least three pitches; one or two means the sample-and-hold is not being clocked

common_mistakes.message: the generator never retriggers, so the patch plays a single note
nothing clocks the sample-and-hold, so every note is the same pitch
the sampled voltage never reaches a pitch input
nothing opens an amplifier, so the notes run together

implies: each harmonic on its own envelope
idioms.is: Several oscillators, each through its own amplifier with its own envelope, summed — so the partials of the sound come and go independently and the timbre is built rather than filtered.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the balance between the partials changes over the note, and no filter is doing it.
idioms.source: Strange on additive synthesis with an independent envelope per partial

topology.describe: each partial has to pass through its own amplifier
an envelope has to control that amplifier — without one the partials cannot move against each other, which is the whole point
the partials have to be summed

listen_for.sounds_like: a tone whose colour shifts from the inside, as though parts of it were being played separately — quite unlike a filter, which moves everything at once and in one direction
listen_for.confusable_with: a drone cluster, where the oscillators are simply summed and their balance is fixed

expect.why: independent envelopes on the partials should move the brightness; a flat centroid means they are all opening together

common_mistakes.message: the partials have no envelopes, so their balance never changes and this is a drone cluster
the partials are never summed
no oscillator passes through an amplifier
